citation: Korakakis V, et al. (2020). Muscle Fiber Composition, Jumping Performance, and Rate of Force Development Adaptations Induced by Different Power Training Volumes in Females. J Strength Cond Res.
population: 29 females (age, training level, sport not reported)
intervention: 10 weeks of eccentric-only power training: 4 fast-velocity eccentric-only half-squats at 70% concentric 1RM followed by 3 maximum countermovement jumps per set, performed as 3 (low), 6 (moderate), or 9 (high) sets per session
outcome_measures: Muscle fiber type percentage (type IIx, type IIa)
summary: This RCT compared three volumes of eccentric-only power training in 29 females over 10 weeks. All groups improved strength, jump performance, rate of force development, and muscle fiber size, but the low-volume group (3 sets/session) achieved greater gains in countermovement jump height/power and early RFD than moderate (6 sets) or high (9 sets) volumes. Moderate and high volumes reduced type IIx fiber percentage while increasing type IIa, and fiber-type shifts correlated with performance changes.
key_findings: All groups increased half-squat 1RM, CMJ height/power, maximum isometric force, RFD, and muscle fiber CSA (p = 0.001).
Low-volume training (3 sets) produced larger increases in CMJ height/power and early RFD than moderate (6 sets) and high (9 sets) volumes (p < 0.001).
Moderate- and high-volume training significantly decreased type IIx fiber percentage and %CSA while increasing type IIa fibers (p = 0.001).
Changes in type IIx/IIa percentages, fiber CSA, and %CSA correlated with performance changes (r = -0.787 to 0.792, p < 0.05).
Early RFD increased after low- or moderate-volume training but not after high-volume training.
effect_size: p = 0.001 for main effects; p < 0.001 for low vs moderate/high volume differences; r = -0.787 to 0.792 for fiber-performance correlations
limitations: Small sample (29 females) limits generalizability; only females studied; 10-week duration may not reflect long-term adaptations; no blinding or randomization details reported; single eccentric-only modality.
